Inlet Medical
Office of the manager

20 August 2026

Sam Nguyen
Night file clerk
Cedar Ridge
Washington

Dear Sam Nguyen,

I am Pat Morales, office manager, Inlet Medical. I am writing to you at Cedar Ridge because the two clinics are to join, and you are the person who sends the Cedar Ridge night file. This letter is the notice from my office. It is not a file, and it does not stand in for one.

Inlet Medical is to merge into Cedar Ridge on 1 September 2026. Both clinics are in Washington. After that date the plan told to this office is that Inlet Medical sits inside Cedar Ridge, and that the night work for the joined clinic is the night work Cedar Ridge already does. I want you to have that date from me, on paper, before the month turns. Tuesday, 1 September, is the morning the offices have been told to use. I am sending this on Thursday, 20 August, so there are working days between the letter and that morning.

Cedar Ridge has no slot API. I am not asking you to build one for the merged clinic, and I am not asking Inlet staff to pretend we have one to hand over. The release you already make is the nightly file, including Saturday and Sunday. That practice is yours. This letter does not change the hours of the night drop, and it does not move the drop onto the Vancouver office week. What I need to put in front of you is the name that will be written on files that already exist.

A historical file id, as my staff use the words, is the id that was written when that night's file was made. Inlet nights have carried ids that begin with the site token inlet-. Cedar Ridge nights, as I understand your practice, carry ids that begin with cedar-. On 1 September those two habits meet. I have been asked, in this building, what happens to a historical file id after the merger. I do not have an answer I am willing to pretend is a rule.

Three descriptions are sitting in the questions people bring me, and I am listing them so you can see that I heard them. One description leaves the historical file id as it was written, so a night that was filed under an inlet- id is still found under that id. Another description stops using that id and writes a cedar- id for the same night. A third description keeps both strings, the old id and a cedar id, on the same night. I have now listed them. Listing them is not a choice. I am not instructing you to keep the old id. I am not instructing you to retire it. I am not instructing you to store both. This letter does not close that question, and I do not want a sentence added under my signature that sounds as if it did.

The site ids I have on the notices are inlet-medical for this office and cedar-ridge for yours. People here sometimes speak of the site id and the file id as if they were the same string. I am not deciding that they are the same string, and I am not deciding that a change to one is a change to the other. If your night file treats them as one token, you will know that better than I do. What I will say from this desk is that nobody has handed me a written rule for historical file ids, and I am not going to invent one in a merger letter twelve days before the date.

Please do not read this as a request to reprint old nights under a new id before 1 September. Please do not read it as a request to freeze the old id in place either. Both of those would be instructions. I am not giving them. If your supervisor at Cedar Ridge has a written rule already, I have not seen it, and I ask you to send me a copy rather than to assume I meant the opposite of whatever it says. If there is no written rule, then the question is still open when you finish this page, which is the state I intend.

My staff will keep typing the ids that are already on the files in this office until someone with authority over both clinics writes a rule down. I am the office manager here. I can tell them a merger date. I cannot tell them a file id they will not be able to find on the morning after the merger, because I have not been given that id. If we meet before 1 September, I will bring the three descriptions and no fourth one that pretends to win. You are welcome to bring the constraints of the night file, including the absence of a slot API and the fact that you file on weekend nights. Those facts are about how Cedar Ridge releases a night. They are not, by themselves, a decision about an id that was written on an earlier night.

I will be at Inlet Medical through the end of August. Correspondence can come to me, Pat Morales, office manager, Inlet Medical. After 1 September I expect to be reached through the Cedar Ridge office, but I do not yet know which door, because that detail is traveling with the same unset question about names. Until a rule exists, use this letter as notice of the merger date and as a statement that historical file ids are still an open question between the offices.

Yours sincerely,

Pat Morales, office manager, Inlet Medical
